 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. "WWE SmackDown" was in Evansville, Indiana, on Friday as Survivor Series: WarGames draws near. The show refused to let off the brakes, hosting five matches over the two-hour window.
 Cup check
 For the second week in a row, a "SmackDown" main-event match ended after a low-blow sequence. Last week Gunther did the kicking , nailing Finn Balor for the win; on Friday night, Balor got his revenge, helping Kevin Owens score the 'W.'
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In terms of star power, this is as quality of a main event for a weekly show as you can ask for, and the stylistic clash between Owens and Gunther tonight was interesting. It worked for the most part, even if Balor's inclusion was expected. What wasn't expected, however, was Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae; the duo were lambasted at the start of the night by Owens, who still promises he'll take the WWE title from Sami Zayn.
 Balor and Zayn got their respective last laughs in the end, signaling impending rematches with their rivals at some point sooner rather than later.
 Obviously Balor and Gunther need a proper stipulation blowoff match themselves after back-to-back nutshots. Steel cup on a pole match, anyone?
 👩‍🦯‍➡️ Blind Referee of the Night
 I've had plenty to say about the kayfabe stupidity of WWE referees this year. The opening match between Charlotte Flair and Jade Cargill once again highlighted it.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement We see turnbuckle spots pretty regularly, and if they happen fast, as we saw in the recent Ethan Page vs. Chad Gable match, it can work perfectly.
 The finish in Friday night's match absolutely was not that.
 Out of desperation, Cargill went to untie the middle turnbuckle before Flair suplexed her across the ring, sending the turnbuckle pad cartoonishly flying through the air. It was impossible not to see that piece of leather ascend to the heavens. Instead of doing literally anything about it, the referee completely ignored it, even after Flair was slammed into it before taking the pin.
 Sometimes these things can be excusable, but for what was an otherwise solid rematch between these two that had interference banned, you'd just like to see an in-kayfabe logic that respects the audience's intelligence. Nonetheless, Cargill and company now have the advantage in next weekend's women's WarGames match.
 👑 Uncrowned Gem of the Night 👑
 A Hacksaw Jim Duggan appearance was not on my 2026 pro-wrestling bingo card, I can tell you that much. Unbelievably, it was the best thing on tonight's whole show, and it wasn't even close. I'm not even kidding; this was actually the funniest segment WWE has produced all year. Maybe in several years.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Continuing to butt heads as the self-proclaimed captains of Team USA, CM Punk and Cody Rhodes met in the ring to discuss their squad's final member, whom Punk welcomed as Duggan. Rhodes wasn't for it at first, and they huddled into the corner, with Duggan chilling in the background as they still spoke into their mics, trying not to break character (and failing) for several minutes. I mean, this was just brilliant on every single level, including Duggan seeing the Team Mexico highlight reel and dipping out.
 Trick Williams came out immediately after as nothing more than a swerve fill-in, which felt kind of unnecessary.
 Tricked
 It was nice to see Damian Priest back in a meaningful match of any kind this week, but it amounted to virtually nothing when he quickly DQ'd himself by hitting Williams in the knee with the ring bell.
 This appears to be a directional shift for Priest into the U.S. title scene, while excusing Williams out of the Survivor Series tag match. Now Rhodes is seemingly hinting that Seth Rollins will be the final member, which Punk will surely not be thrilled about.
 Remember him?
 Kit Wilson wrestled Rey Fenix, and it reminded me of one thing. This dude was getting over pretty well with crowds when he started the "Toxic" gimmick.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Then he was just thrown into the Danhausen bin and disappeared.
 WWE really can't accept people getting over organically, but this match was a good display of how good Wilson is. The jumping elbow he does outside the ring always looks great.
 Monroe Mania
 Blake Monroe still isn't doing much of anything since she finished her feud with Giulia weeks ago. But it's nice to see her involved with the women's title scene — and with Chelsea Green, who Monroe is seemingly destined to have a match with. It admittedly feels pretty out of place right now with Tiffany Stratton still linked to Green, but it's a good spot for Monroe nonetheless.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ideally, WWE just wouldn't have gone this route with the Money in the Bank briefcase, but it's too late for that now.
 I give Friday's "SmackDown" a crown score of: 👑 6.5/10 👑
